latest_nl_proof:
Let m = floor(p/4). By the defining property of the floor function, we have

m <= p/4 < m + 1.

From the right-hand inequality p/4 < m + 1, subtract 1 from both sides to get

p/4 - 1 < m,

that is,

m > p/4 - 1.

Now the hypothesis says n >= floor(p/4) = m. Therefore n >= m > p/4 - 1. By transitivity of the order relation, we conclude

n > p/4 - 1.

This proves the statement.
role_in_parent: Converts the integer lower bounds proved in the residue-class lemmas into the exact strict inequality required by the root theorem.
statement_nl: Let p be an integer and let n be an integer. If n >= floor(p/4), then n > p/4 - 1.

domain_restrictions: floor(p/4) is the integer given by the floor function applied to the real number p/4
comparisons (>=, >) are standard order relations on real numbers (identifying integers with reals)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all p ∈ Z and for all n ∈ Z, if n ≥ floor(p/4) then n > p/4 - 1.
witness_dependencies: floor(p/4) is an integer-valued expression depending on p (no existential witness introduced)
no existential quantifiers appear; n is arbitrary/universal, not a witness
